# Heuristic Investigation

## Individual Heuristic Investigation

attempt at using heuristics to predict asset grades on case by case basis
	- identify the specific assets
	- find them on google maps and the AIMS spatial flood defences interactive map
	- find all information needed for the heuristic inputs for that asset. for example:
		- use satellite images to identify the material of the asset
		- for embankments, use vertical images to try and identify whether the asset had a reinforced base or not
		- download lidar dmt 5m data for the tiles containing the assets, and by combining with satellite images use qgis to draw the elevation profile at a cross section of the embankment. Use this to determine narrow or wide embankments
		- double check fluvial vs coastal vs tidal environment, making a judgement call. It was clear that assuming that all assets in the register called tidal were coastal did not hold, but there was no other information available to make a well informed decision. This must be part of the local expertise that is mentioned in halcrow
	- reject assets where good enough information cannot be compiled. For example, where street view was not available to identify the material of a wall, or where the vertical images could not help determine whether an embankment was reenforced or not.
		- i need to mention the rejection rate - its very high. It will be important to show that using the heuristics is not feasible for the whole national dataset
	- use assets with full data to make a prediction of its grade, using those collected characteristics and the estimated age of the asset. 
	- calculate simple metrics about the success of predicting this way. These are not the full metrics that are used in other experiments since this is a narrative exercise - the point is to show that using heuristics on the entire national register of assets is not feasible, and the results are incomparable to the nationally scoped attempts. 

![Individual Asset Heuristic Investigation](figures/IndividualFloodDefenceAssetHeuristicsPrediction.drawio.pdf){#fig-indi-heuristic-flow }

A research task was designed and undertaken to faithfully use the heuristics specified in the Halcrow document to produce high quality predictions. Since it was anticipated that this would be intensive and open ended, this was a time boxed task. The major caveate to this task is that Halcrow calls for expertice and local knowledge to be applied during implementation, and the author is not an expert flood defence engineer. That said, best effort was made to apply sound judgement, and when in doubt to remove uncertain data from the set that was collected instead of using assumptions. 

The task to lasted several days and produced only a very modest output - only 11 high confidence assets. Full outputs of the collected data and the filtered selection are in notebook 8.
